question: Will any political party or coalition acquire a supermajority in the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary elections?

forecasts.reference-class: Historical base rate of obtaining a constitutional two-thirds majority (133/199 seats) in Hungary's parliamentary elections since 1990; two-thirds has been achieved in 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022 but not in several earlier cycles.

sources.claim: Hungary Today cites Real-PR polling with a seat-calculator projection implying Fidesz-KDNP could secure around two-thirds of parliamentary seats (roughly 64% of seats), indicating a plausible near-two-thirds majority.

Euronews summarizes multiple polls showing split outcomes (Tisza leading in several surveys) and notes prediction-market signals where odds favored the opposition, illustrating uncertainty about a guaranteed two-thirds majority.
AP News reports the election date as April 12, 2026 and notes that most independent polls at the time show Tisza ahead of Fidesz, highlighting uncertainty about a governing two-thirds majority.

The Budapest Times cites analysts who argued that the 2024 European Parliament results would translate into a two-thirds majority in a general election, indicating that such an outcome is plausible under certain electoral dynamics.

The Financial Times notes the opposition is consolidating around the Tisza party and that polls show Tisza leading, signaling a potentially reduced risk of a guaranteed two-thirds majority for the ruling bloc.
Real-PR seat projection suggests Fidesz–KDNP would win around 64 percent of parliamentary seats, implying a government majority near two-thirds.
Polymarket odds show Magyar (Tisza) leading at 57% vs. Orbán at 39%; betting markets tilt toward the opposition in this polling landscape.
Nézőpont Institute analysis from EP results suggested a national translation could yield roughly 135 seats for Fidesz–KDNP, i.e., a two-thirds majority under certain assumptions.
Background notes that Fidesz has won two-thirds majorities in 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022; the 2026 race remains uncertain and subject to polling and coalition dynamics.
Publicus Research (Feb 15, 2026) shows TISZA 48%, Fidesz 39%; projected composition: Fidesz 102, TISZA 85, MH 12 — no 133-seat majority.
Republikon poll (Feb 17, 2026) shows TISZA 47%, Fidesz 39%, MH 6%, DK 3%; projected seats: TISZA 107, Fidesz 82, MH 10.
Nézőpont poll (Feb 11, 2026) shows Fidesz 46%, TISZA 40%, MH 7%, DK 4%; projected seats: TISZA 107, Fidesz 82, MH 10.
Euronews summarizes multiple February 2026 polls; leads vary and none consistently indicate a path to a 2/3 majority.
Hungary Today notes a Real-PR seat projection around two-thirds for Fidesz-KDNP in one model, though other polls show divergent results.
Závecz Research (Nov 30, 2025) shows TISZA leading 47% to 38% for Fidesz.
